- Tool results accept images, videos and mixed content through the existing native media pipeline and Qwen tool-response wrapper.
- Matching preceding tool calls, unique result IDs, a real user query, request-wide media limits and existing local/remote source policies remain required.
- Media-only results count as payload. Explicit original text/JSON errors remain failures even when accompanied by media and cannot reopen an exhausted retry window.
- Text-only behavior, thinking defaults, safe-prefix implementation and GPU arithmetic are unchanged.

## Client integration

Client SDKs and gateways must also accept tool content arrays. Existing exhausted-tool responses remain HTTP 400 with `error.code=tool_call_no_progress`, or an SSE error followed by `[DONE]` without a successful terminal `finish_reason`.

These engine checks do not claim acceptance of the original partner Harness end-to-end workflow. Original private sessions and documents are not included.

v1.5.1-native-vl.9 — tool recovery and document diagnostics

This patch addresses the confirmed engine-side failure modes in the 0911 agent feedback.

The unpublished `.8` candidate was blocked by its package documentation check.
`.9` includes the missing feedback document and caller checker, verified by a
Linux copy/executable regression. The old local candidate tag is not moved;
the native engine bytes and measured prefix/text candidate are unchanged.

- Completed repairs reopen the retry window for identical verification commands, including a different command that succeeds without stdout.
- Lifetime failure metrics are retained; a new current-window streak controls the retry limit. Replayed result IDs are rejected and late/parallel result ordering cannot manufacture progress.
- If every proposed tool call is exhausted, the engine returns an explicit error rather than ordinary completion. Mixed responses retain other admitted calls.
- A caller-side DOCX checker detects text with a .docx suffix, missing files and malformed containers. Optional Markdown recovery does not turn invalid DOCX into a passing artifact.

## Client integration notice
